title: Astro Next network endpoint manifest
description: Every host the product may contact, with its disposition.
The host set is NOT typed by hand. tools/policy/endpoint_seed.py derives it by importing
tools/baseline/inventory_endpoints.py -- issue #6's generator, which CI already checks
against docs/astro-next/baseline/network-inventory.yaml -- and adds a scan of webui/, which
that generator does not read. tools/policy/manifest.py then joins this file against the seed
STRICTLY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: a seeded host with no entry fails, and an entry naming a host
the seed does not produce fails unless it declares itself `declared` with a reason.
So this file holds judgement only. It cannot silently fall behind the repository, because
the half that can be derived is derived on every run.
DECLARED, not measured here. Baseline finding 3 records nine Astro patches that do not
apply to the locked Chromium revision, so a host their text ADDS is in no tree today.
Measuring it needs a Chromium checkout and a patch run; this module deliberately needs
neither. The validator checks only that each named patch still exists in the series, so a
rename fails loudly -- a patch whose apply status CHANGES will not, and that limit is
stated here rather than left for a reader to discover.
What the CURRENT build does about this host, separate from the decision, for the
same reason the feature manifest separates them: an inherited patch's effect must
never be readable as a decision somebody took.
This axis is what makes DISABLE_BUILD and DISABLE_RUNTIME falsifiable rather than
rhetorical. `REMOVED_BY_PATCH` says the literal is absent from the tree, which a
string scan of the artefact can check. `RUNTIME_BLOCKED` says the literal is
PRESENT and the request is stopped elsewhere -- for the 20 hosts the inherited
iridium patch rewrites to `trk:`, the calling code is still compiled and still
reached, and only the net layer refuses. Those two look identical in a feature list
and are entirely different in a threat model.
`NOT_BUILT` is neither: baseline finding 1 measured that nothing links the Astro
overlay into the build graph, so every Astro-owned endpoint is absent from today's
binary through a build defect owned by #7, not through any disposition.

host.description: Exactly as the seed produces it. The join is on this string.

id.description: Stable endpoint id. Generated constants and tests reference this, never a raw URL.

owning_feature.description: A feature id from the feature manifest, or `none` for a reference that owns nothing.

description: WHY the host appears in committed text. The single most load-bearing field, because
the seed finds strings and only some strings are requests.
request-literal    code builds a request from it
csp-allowlist      a Content-Security-Policy source expression; permits a request,
is not one, and may permit a host nothing calls
default-content    shipped default data a user may act on (an NTP tile, a DoH
template, a search engine choice) -- user-initiated, not automatic
help-link          a URL rendered as a clickable link in product UI
documentation      a comment, a translator note, a `<ex>` placeholder; never fetched
deleted-by-patch   present ONLY on removed lines: the patched tree does not contain it
blocklist-literal  named in order to be blocked, rewritten or prefixed
filename           a diff header, not a URL at all
not-a-host         a format string the URL scan matched (`%s%s`, `%s:%d`)
Whether the product contacts this host, and on whose initiative. Orthogonal to
`state`: a DISABLE_RUNTIME endpoint is still `automatic` if the code that would call
it is compiled in, which is exactly why DISABLE_RUNTIME may not be asserted as
'cannot happen'.

wildcard_justification.description: Required for any host containing `*`. Wildcards are otherwise rejected.

http_justification.description: Required for scheme `http` on a production endpoint. Otherwise rejected.

release_blocked.description: Required true for any staging or local-test endpoint: a release build may not contain it.

description: Required for an entry the seed does not produce. Says why the host cannot be derived
from committed text -- typically an upstream Chromium endpoint no Astro patch
mentions, which the baseline inventory cannot see because it scans Astro's overlay
and patch text only.
